sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Public entry point for the client
sections.what: Gathers the client's exports so apps can import them from one place.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps apps from depending on the internal file layout.
sections.watch_out: The generated exports are passed through wholesale, so any new name added to the generated files appears here automatically.

summary: The public front door of the API client, gathering the generated API calls, their validation schemas, and the two setup functions into one import point.
purpose: Lets other code import everything from a single place.
why: Likely reason: hides the internal file layout from the apps that use the client.
how: Re-exports the generated API calls and schemas, and re-exports the base address and token setup functions along with the token type.
inputs: The files in the generated folder and the custom-fetch file.
outputs: A set of named exports for other packages.
risks: The generated files are not shown in the packet. Renaming something in them changes what this file exposes, and duplicate names across the export statements would conflict.
debug: If an import is missing, check that the generated folder exists and was regenerated after the last schema change.
